A Stranger's Heart

I came across an odd stranger inside Mordrin Hanin's Tomb. He asked me to return his heart to him so that he may move on to the next life. To do that, I need to challenge the Storm Monarch guarding Mordrin Hanin's burial chamber. I accepted.

I came across an odd stranger inside Mordrin Hanin's Tomb. He asked me to return his heart to him so that he may move on to the next life. To do that, I need to challenge the Storm Monarch guarding Mordrin Hanin's burial chamber. I denyed the request. The stranger told me to come back, if I change my mind.

I returned to the stranger inside Mordrin Hanin's Tomb and told him I had changed my mind. I will help him retrieve his heart so that he may move on. I will need to face the Storm Monarch guarding Mordrin Hanin's burial chamber to claim the heart.
I claimed the stranger's heart from the Storm Monarch. I should return it to the stranger and see what he can tell me about this strange place.
I defeated the Storm Monarch inside Mordrin Hanin's Tomb and found a well preserved heart on its body. I wonder who might be missing a heart, because it clearly does not belong to the Storm Monarch.

I returned the heart to the stranger. He was greatful and looking forward to finally leaving Mordrin Hanin's Tomb behind. In return for my service, he offerd to answer all my questions as best he could.

I returned the heart to a strange person inside Mordrin Hanin's Tomb. The stranger said that with the heart he was finally able to leave the tomb behind. In return for my service, he offerd to answer all my questions as best he could.
The Wake of Hanin

I found a sorceress named Elante in an old cave scattered with daedric fragments. She asked me to look for her associate Badama and a "Key Guardian", but I declined. She told me to come back to her, if I change my mind.

I found a sorceress named Elante in an old cave scattered with daedric fragments. She asked me to look for her associate Badama and a "Key Guardian". I accepted. Badrama must be somewhere inside these caves.

I found Badama and the key in Ibar-Dad. Badama was already dead. When bringing the news to Elante she didn't seem very upset. All she wanted was to open that door. She told me that if I venture on deeper into the caves, we are sure to meet again.

I met a sorceress named Elante in Ibar-Dad. She asked me, if I had come across her acossiate, Badama. As a matter of fact, I had. I had also taken the key that Elante sent Badama to find. Elante seemed unconcerned about her associate's passing and asked me to open the door behind her. She said we would surely meet again, if I chose to venture onwards.

I caught up with Elante deep inside Ibar-Dad. She told me that there was a sort of gateway to the tomb of Mordrin Hanin. To access the tomb, one has to drink a special potion, the Cup of Passage, in that particular place. Elante said that the potion needed to be brewed over the bones of traitors and that my blood was the final ingredient she needed. She attacked me.
Elante is dead. I should check her corpse for anything interesting.

I completed the Cup of Passage and drank it. I was transported to a new location. According to Elante, this must be Mordrin Hanin's Tomb. It seems that levitation does not work in this place. Nor can I teleport home. The only way is forward.
I completed the Cup of Passage and drank it. I was transported to a new location. It seems that levitation does not work in this place. Nor can I teleport home. The only way is forward.

In Mordrin Hanin's tomb I found many statues that depict many Daedric Princes. When I touched the crystal in front of Mehrunes Dagon's statue the Daedric Prince seemed pleased. Perhaps I should touch the crystals in front of the other statues. But in what order?
When I touched the crystal in front of Mephala's statue the Daedric Prince seemed pleased.
When I touched the crystal in front of Molag Bal's statue the Daedric Prince seemed pleased.
When I touched the crystal in front of Namira's statue the Daedric Prince seemed pleased.
When I touched the crystal in front of Malacath's statue the Daedric Prince seemed pleased.
When I touched the crystal in front of Sanguine's statue the Daedric Prince seemed pleased.
When I touched the crystal in front of Boethia's statue the Daedric Prince seemed pleased.
When I touched the crystal in front of Hircine's statue the Daedric Prince seemed pleased.
When I touched the crystal in front of Hermaeus Mora's statue the Daedric Prince seemed pleased.
When I touched the crystal in front of Sheogorath's statue the Daedric Prince seemed pleased.
When I touched the crystal in front of Azura's statue the Daedric Prince seemed pleased. I touched all of the crystals in the correct order it seems. Now what?

There is one more crystal in front of a large door. After touching all other crystals in the correct order I touched the last crystal and the door opened. Behind it, Mordrin Hanin's resting place. All his treasure shall now be mine. But how do I get out of this place?
Outside Mordrin Hanin's burial chamber, I was approached by a bodyless being that apologized for past transgressions. It gave me a ring that will get me out of this place and back.
Yes, yes, the musicians. I have met them. They are quite chatty.
It is very strange, isn't it?

Thank you, thank you! Now, I promised to answer your questions about this very strange place. I have knowledge and speculation ... a dangerous combination, but it's the best I can give. Perhaps you want to know more about the mighty Storm Monarch? Or about my fate? Or do you wish to know who Mordrin Hanin truly was? The many statues play a part in that. Then there is the odd shipwreck down below, have you seen it? And, of course, the musicians and their sweet tune. Ask away, my friend, for I am yours.

It is indeed. I came here a long time ago, and, like you I presume, I sought to locate the burial chamber of the great Mordrin Hanin. I came close, but alas, I wasn't worthy. The Storm Monarch guarding the chamber crushed my body. I have been stuck here ever since, unable to move on. Until now. Please, friernd, give me back my heart, so that I may finally leave this place, and, perhaps, meet the great Mordrin Hanin in the next life. In exchange, I am willing to share my knowledge with you.
It is, isn't it? And even stranger now ... I smell an odd scent on you. Tell me, friend, do you carry my heart with you?

Now, as I recall, I promised to answer your questions about this very strange place. I have knowledge and speculation ... a dangerous combination, but it's the best I can give. Perhaps you want to know more about the mighty Storm Monarch? Or about my fate? Or do you wish to know who Mordrin Hanin truly was? The many statues play a part in that. Then there is the odd shipwreck down below, have you seen it? And, of course, the musicians and their sweet tune. Ask away, my friend, for I am yours.
You brought me my heart ... friend, I am so grateful. Thank you, thank you! I may finally leave this place and move on. Perhaps, I shall finally meet the great Mordrin Hanin.
Well, if you change your mind, I'm not going anywhere ...

Thank you, my friend! I am certain the Storm Monarch still has my heart in its clutches. Do be careful, friend. The Monarch is no easy foe, and it will crush anyone who does not prove themselves worthy.
So, friend ... have you changed your mind? Will you challenge the Storm Monarch and claim back my heart?
How cruel you are, for denying me salvation. Well, I'm not going anywhere. If you change your mind ...

I have no power here. The body you see in front of you is a husk filled with nothing but regret. Thus, the Storm Monarch cannot harm me anymore. Nor I it. You will have to face the Storm Monarch anyway, if you want to enter the great Hanin's burial chamber. Please, my friend, save my heart and give it back to me, so I may finally move on. What say you?

I came here a long time ago, and, like you I presume, I sought to locate the burial chamber of Mordrin the Great. I came close, but alas, I wasn't worthy. The Storm Monarch guarding the chamber crushed my body. I have been stuck here ever since, unable to move on. My friend, if you bring me back my heart, then I can finally leave this place, and perhaps find the great Hanin in the next life. In return, you may ask me anything you want to know about this strange place.
It is, isn't it? Say, I was wondering, if you could do me a favor. I don't have much to offer in return, except my knowledge.

Ah yes, the mighty Storm Monarch, a sight to behold, isn't it? The Elders who entombed the great Mordrin Hanin in this place summoned the Storm Monarch and the other Daedra to protect the burial chamber. The Elders must have been particularly powerful, for it is not easy to control a Storm Monarch and bind it to this world. Then again, are we still in "this" world?

That is why I took Badama along. Although I now realize that I should never have sent her off to search for the key. But as luck would have it, I was sent a replacement. The final ingredient is the blood of a traitor. I thank you, stranger. You have been very helpful.

I prepared the potion as far as I could. Unfortunately, I was lacking a key ingredient as well as the proper means to heat the mixture. No more. This pyre is fueled by the bones of traitors. It is where I must brew the potion once I gathered the final ingredient.

It is a special potion. One mixed long ago to give Mordrin Hanin companions on his journey into death. Perhaps you are familiar with the book "Hanin's Wake". In it, it is detailed how to brew the potion. However, the book does not tell you the whole truth. It neglects to mention the secret use of the Cup of Passage. It neglects to mention that when you drink the potion in this specific place, it will grant you access to Mordrin Hanin's tomb ... and all the treasure it hides.

Indeed. It may not look it, but this is the place where I can pass over to Hanin's tomb to claim its treasure. All I need do is drink the Cup of Passage. In any other place, the drink would kill me, condemning me to be an eternal companion of the great Hanin in whatever world comes next. But here, the Cup of Passage will allow me to be transported ... to move on.

Yes, the great Mordrin Hanin's tomb is waiting for me. I am given to understand that it is a marvelous and majestic place, full of wonders and full of beauty. I wish to see it with my own eyes ... and I wish to claim the treasures that Mordrin Hanin is said to be buried with. My colleages at the Mages Guild spurned me for my obsession, but I have prevailed. This is the gateway, I am sure of it.

Yes, the great Mordrin Hanin's tomb. I am given to understand that it is a marvelous and majestic place, full of wonders and full of beauty. I wish to see it with my own eyes ... and I wish to claim the treasures that Mordrin Hanin is said to be buried with. My colleages at the Mages Guild spurned me for my obsession, but I have prevailed. This is the gateway that will take me to the tomb, I am sure of it.

Yes, the many statues ... Witnesses to the great Mordrin Hanin's funeral, for when Mordrin died, even the gods shed their tears. Or so the stories tell. The Elders who buried old Modrin were a group of powerful Daedra worshippers, and they came from renowned places, such as Ashalmawia, Maelkashishi and Ald Sotha. Notice the absence of five commonly known Daedric Princes. Vaermina, Clavicus Vile, Peryite, Meridia and Nocturnal, all missing. Considered traitors by the Elders. Why? I do not know.

Ah, you did not come here by your own doing, did you? A woman named Elante paved the way for you ... curious that she should perish while you go on to reap the rewards. Then again, perhaps she wasn't worthy, just like myself. Perhaps she isn't truly gone either. Maybe, just maybe, we shall see her again ...

The odd shipwreck lies at the bottom of this cavern. How did it get here? For you and I both know that the only way to reach this strange place is through the Traitor's Flame. No boat could make the trip. Or so it would seem. Perhaps they found another way. Then again, it is said that drinking the Cup of Passage in any place other than in front of the Traitor's Flame will kill you. And it would seem that the ship's crew all perished. So perhaps, in a way, the legends have been proven right.

Who was Mordrin Hanin, truly? He died so long ago that his passing has become the stuff of legend. Who he was remains an enigma. Perhaps he was a powerful priest worshipping one of the Daedra. Some, in fact, claim that Mordrin may have been involved with a cult of Mehrunes Dagon worshippers. Then there is evidence that Mordrin was actually a Nord noble from Skyrim. Or maybe he was something else entirely. We do not know. All the more reason for the likes of us to seek his tomb and find a hint of the truth.
I ... am ... sorry ...
My friend, is there one more thing?
You have returned, friend. A strange place this is, oh yes, strange and beautiful, but I am ready to move on. How did you fare against the Storm Monarch?
Please be careful when chellenging the Storm Monarch, lest it crush your body as it did mine.
Have you changed your mind, friend? A strange place this is, yes. I want to leave.
Greetings, friend. A strange place this is, isn't it?
We will meet again soon, I expect.
Ah, you have made it. As expected. I am sure this is the place. This is the gateway to Mordrin Hanin's tomb.
How rude of you to just brush past me like that. Of course I would follow you and overtake you, you silly thing. Do you at least understand where we are? This is the gateway to Mordrin Hanin's Tomb.
You have returned. What of Badama ... and the key?
I suggest you get moving. Go look for Badama ... and the key.
Back again, stranger? Have you changed your mind? Will you look for Badama?

Greetings, stranger. You are the one who unlocked the door, aren't you? I take it that means that my trusted associate Badama was not up to the task. Pity. You on the other hand proved yourself quite capable. You, too, then are searching for Mordrin Hanin's Tomb I take it.
Greetings, stranger. What brings you here? You wouldn't happen to have come across my associate, Badama?

I thought it was my fate to enter Mordrin Hanin's burial chamber and bask in his greatness. Alas, I was unworthy. Now I believe it is my fate to move on and find Mordrin Hanin in the next life. I will be gone soon and perish in your wake, for you are the one who is meant to enter the chamber and find the great Mordrin Hanin. I can see that now. If you have need of it, you may have my old glass katana. If you can find it. It must have fallen down the waterfall after the Storm Monarch crushed my body.

Really? Interesting. It seems my faith in Badama and her abilities was misplaced. Then go ahead and open that door, stranger. If you seek to venture on and find out what lies hidden in these caves, then I am sure we will meet again.
So you do. Now, open that door please. If you seek to venture on and find out what lies hidden in these caves, then I am sure we will meet again.
So Badama is dead ... such a silly child. I had full faith in her abilities, but it seems that faith was misplaced. You on the other hand ... you have managed to retrieve the key, haven't you?
Badama is my associate. I have special need of her. Although I wonder ...
Excellent. I suggest you be on your way then. Badama can't be far.
That is unfortunate. Let me know, if you change your mind.
Yes, will you look for Badama and the key to this door?
Might I ask you to look for her then? And the key? Without it, we will not be getting through this door.

Yes, she is my associate. Together, we have been excavating these caves. I sent her off to look for the fabled "Key Guardian" and take whatever key it is guarding. A task Badama should be more than adequate for. However, she has not yet returned. Have you seen her?
